subject: Post-demo: Skyline integration, SDK auth and 5xx triage
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Michael Wu <michael.wu@skylinehealth.com>, eng@skylinehealth.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: next steps + logs request

Michael / Skyline team — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and what we said we'd do next: 

- Recap: You showed request flow (frontend -> backend -> Redwood SDK -> /v1/generate). You saw intermittent 502/5xx responses during burst tests.
- Immediate asks from our side: 1) SDK version and initialization snippet, 2) a minimal payload sample that triggers the 5xx, and 3) server logs / request IDs for the failing requests.
- Redwood next steps: We'll attempt to reproduce on a sandbox we share and check routing + auth headers that could cause fallback routing to the shared pool. Connor will take the lead on repro steps; I'll coordinate with infra if needed.

Can you attach the payload sample and any error IDs? If you prefer, drop them in the HubSpot deal or the Drive link below. Also propose a brief follow-up on Thursday to review repro progress.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Phone: (415) 555-0194

Attachments referenced: payload-sample.json (please attach the payload that reproduces the 5xx)

From: Michael Wu <michael.wu@skylinehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Skyline Eng Team <eng@skylinehealth.com>, sec@skylinehealth.com
Date: 2027-02-11T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: next steps + logs request

Hi Naomi — attaching two items inline: short payload that triggered the error and a minimal server-side log snippet. We saw ~30% of burst requests returning 502/504 around 10:17–10:24 PST. Excerpt from our logs: 

[2027-02-11T10:17:23Z] request_id=sky-84a1 endpoint=/v1/generate status=502 upstream_error="map[string]..."
[2027-02-11T10:17:45Z] request_id=sky-84a9 endpoint=/v1/embeddings status=504 timeout

Payload that reproduces: payload-sample.json (attached). We are on your Node SDK v1.2.0 (installed via npm), init using the standard API key. We did add a client-side retry wrapper — could that be causing duplicate KV cache entries?

Let us know if you need anything else — happy to stand up a short session where we share screens.

—Michael
Senior Engineering Manager, Skyline Health
Attachments: payload-sample.json

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Michael Wu <michael.wu@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-12T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: next steps + logs request

Thanks Michael — this is useful. A few quick requests to help us reproduce locally: 

1) Can you confirm the exact SDK install (npm ls | grep redwood-sdk) and the initialization snippet (redact keys)?
2) If you have the full request_id for any failing request (e.g. sky-84a1), share the header X-Redwood-Request-Id if present.
3) Try toggling verbose mode on the SDK (export REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1) and capture a 30s trace.

Short repro steps I'm going to run on our side:
- Run the payload-sample.json with Node v18 + redwood-sdk v1.2.0; try with and without the retry wrapper.
- Inspect the Authorization header and routing decision recorded in our trace.

I've attached a small log we asked other customers to provide (sdk-integration-log.txt) — it contains the headers we need. If you can run the payload through a curl with -v and paste the output, that'll speed things up.

We'll also check for any structured-call/tool-calling payloads that might push a large nested JSON (embedding + reranker combo) over our default timeout. I'll report back by EOD 2/12.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: sdk-integration-log.txt

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Michael Wu <michael.wu@skylinehealth.com>, eng@skylinehealth.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-14T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: next steps + logs request

Michael — quick update from our side after initial repro attempts: 

- We attempted to run the payload against an isolated sandbox we control; we saw the same 502 pattern when requests were routed to a shared inference pool during short capacity bursts. The root cause looks like a routing fallback combined with a higher-than-normal payload size (embedding + reranker together).
- Connor has asked infra to give a deeper trace; infra asked for packet capture to correlate upstream metrics — can you grant permission to post the pcap to the Drive link or attach directly? If you prefer, we can accept a sanitized pcap.

Planned next steps: 
1) Naomi: schedule a 30-min triage with infra + Skyline on Tue 2/16 10am PST — I’ll send a calendar invite.
2) Connor/Ben: run a canary in our sandbox with increased per-request timeout + trunk routing to verify mitigation.
3) Skyline: share the pcap or confirm we can pull trace from your side.

HubSpot deal note: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/78421
Drive trace folder: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/infra/skyline-traces/trace-78421

Thanks — Naomi

P.S. Marissa — looping you for SLA/contract considerations if this needs Reserved/Dedicated capacity.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Wu <michael.wu@skylinehealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-16T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: next steps + logs request

Michael / team — quick engineering note after running the sandbox canary: we reproduced the 5xx behavior. Short summary: 

- Trigger: combined payload with an embeddings call followed immediately by a reranker structured-call inside the same request (large nested JSON ~1.6MB).
- Symptom: routing fallback to shared pool when per-connection concurrency spikes; upstream backend returns 502 under resource pressure.
- Immediate mitigation we tested successfully in sandbox: bump request timeout from 10s to 30s for this endpoint and enable per-request routing affinity (pin to a dedicated worker) for heavy payloads. Also trimming the payload (send embeddings in smaller batches) eliminated the 502s.

Action items: 
1) Ben/Connor: prepare a small client patch that increases SDK default timeout for generate()/structuredCall() when payload > 512KB; we'll open PR for SDK v1.2.1.
2) Naomi: propose a short SOW for Dedicated capacity evaluation if Skyline expects sustained heavy batch workloads.
3) Michael: if you can confirm test results with the adjusted timeout, we'll proceed with a canary rollout.

If you authorize Redwood to apply routing affinity for DL-78421 on a short-term canary, we can schedule the rollout tonight and revert if anything degrades. Please reply with yes/no.

—Ben Carter
Senior Software Engineer, Platform Reliability | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

> Ben / Naomi — thanks for the quick turnaround. We ran an ad-hoc test with 30s timeout and saw no 502s over ~500 requests. Happy to proceed with the canary.
>
> —Michael
